title: From Grey-Box to Green-Box: When can Physics-Informed Machine Learning Reduce Carbon Footprints in Structural Health Monitoring?
abstract: arXiv:2609.33387v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Machine learning plays an increasingly vital role in engineering, but the corresponding increase in compute time is not without environmental cost. Physics-informed machine learning or "grey-box" models have been developed to overcome some of the limitations of traditional black-box learners, utilising the physical insight that an engineer would have about the structure they are modelling and have shown promising results in the structural engineering field among many others. This work explores whether an additional advantage could be a reduced environmental impact, considering the relationship between training data quantity and training time, linking this duration to carbon emissions from computing. translated_title: 从灰箱到绿箱：物理信息机器学习何时能减少结构健康监测中的碳足迹？
translated_abstract: 机器学习在工程领域发挥着日益重要的作用，但随之而来的计算时间增加并非没有环境代价。物理信息机器学习或“灰箱”模型旨在克服传统黑箱学习器的部分局限性，其利用工程师对所建模结构的物理洞察，已在结构工程等众多领域展现出可喜的成果。本研究探讨了此类模型能否带来一项额外优势——降低环境影响，其中考虑了训练数据量与训练时间之间的关系，并将训练时长与计算产生的碳排放相关联。在结构健康监测的背景下，本文评估了四种跨越高斯过程和神经网络的物理信息机器学习方法：残差建模、输入增广、混合建模以及约束学习……
tldr: 本文探讨物理信息机器学习（灰箱模型）能否在结构健康监测中降低碳足迹，通过评估残差建模、输入增广、混合建模和约束学习四种方法，将训练数据量、训练时间与计算碳排放联系起来。
en_tdlr: This paper investigates whether physics-informed machine learning ("grey-box" models) can reduce carbon footprints in structural health monitoring by evaluating four approaches—residual modelling, input augmentation, hybrid modelling, and constrained learning—linking training data quantity and training time to computing-related carbon emissions.
